explain.say: How much water did you drink today? Maybe two litres. But how much water was used to grow your food? Far, far more! Look at the board. The bars show the hidden water, called virtual water, needed to make one kilogram of each food.

faq.a: Virtual water is the water used to make food or other products, hidden inside them. The idea was developed by the geographer John Anthony Allan in the 1990s.

faq.q: Why does beef need so much water?
faq.a: Most of the water goes into growing the grain and grass a cow eats over about three years. The cow’s drinking water and cleaning add a little more.
asks: How much water is in a burger?
How much water does it take to make beef?

faq.q: Why does chocolate need so much water?
faq.a: Cocoa trees grow slowly and give only a small amount of beans each year, so a lot of rain falls on the trees for each kilogram of cocoa. Most of that is rainwater rather than water from taps or rivers.
asks: How much water is in a chocolate bar?

faq.a: A water footprint is the total fresh water used to make everything a person, company or country uses, including hidden water in food, clothes and electricity.
asks: How can I reduce my water footprint?
Which foods use the most water?

faq.q: Why do dry countries import food?
faq.a: Growing thirsty crops uses a lot of scarce water, so dry countries can save their own water by buying those crops from wetter places. Egypt is one of the world’s biggest buyers of wheat.

facts: Producing 1 kg of beef takes on average about 15,400 litres of water (Water Footprint Network).
1 kg of chocolate has a water footprint of about 17,000 litres.
The idea of virtual water was developed by geographer John Anthony Allan in the 1990s.
